title: Getting Help from Public Services
tagline: Where to go, what to bring, and how to follow up.
description: Learn how to find the right office for a service, what papers to prepare, and what to do when your request takes too long. Practical steps for everyday needs like an NRC, a clinic card or a market stand.
outcomes: Know which office handles which service
Prepare the right documents before you go
Ask clearly and keep a record
Follow up politely when help is delayed
Know who to turn to next if you are stuck

lessons.title: Which office does what
lessons.body:
Different needs are handled by different offices. Knowing where to go first saves you time and money.

## Common places
The local council handles markets, rubbish, trading licences and many community services. A health facility handles clinic cards and health services. The civic registration office handles the National Registration Card (NRC) and births. Your ward councillor can help with local problems and point you to the right office.

## Start with the right door
If you are not sure, ask at the office reception or ask your ward councillor. Going to the right place first means fewer trips.
key_points: The council handles markets, rubbish and trading licences
Your ward councillor can point you the right way
lessons.try_it: Think of one service you need. Write down which office is most likely to handle it.

lessons.title: What to bring and how to ask
lessons.body:
Most offices ask for the same few things. Bringing them the first time avoids being turned away.

## Prepare your papers
Carry your NRC. Bring any forms, letters or receipts that relate to your request, and bring copies as well as the originals. If someone is helping you, bring a letter from them.

## Ask clearly
Say what you need in one sentence. Ask for the name of the officer helping you and write it down. Ask how long it will take and what the next step is.
key_points: Carry your NRC and bring copies of papers
Say what you need in one clear sentence
Ask how long it will take
lessons.try_it: Before your next visit, make a small checklist of the papers you will carry.

lessons.title: When help is delayed
lessons.body:
Sometimes a request takes longer than expected. Staying calm and keeping records helps you follow up well.

## A real situation
You applied for a service two weeks ago and heard nothing. What do you do? Go back, or call, and give your reference or the officer's name. Ask politely what stage your request is at and when it will be ready.

## Keep a record
Write the date, who you spoke to and what they said each time. If it is still stuck, ask who the supervisor is, or ask your ward councillor to help you follow up.
key_points: Follow up calmly and give your reference
Ask what stage your request is at
Ask for a supervisor or your councillor if stuck
lessons.try_it: Make a simple note page: date, person, what they said. Use it next time you follow up.
